problemStatement: Harden the URL shortener's operational resilience without new infrastructure: protect link creation from abuse with rate limiting, expose a readiness probe that reflects database connectivity, propagate correlation ids, return consistent problem responses for every error path, and prove graceful shutdown and transient-error retry of the click writer - all while keeping existing behaviour and tests intact.
functionalRequirements: FR1: POST /api/links is rate limited per fixed one-minute window; excess requests receive 429 Too Many Requests. Redirects and reads are not limited.
FR2: GET /health/ready returns 200 when the database is reachable and 503 with problem details when it is not; GET /health stays a pure liveness check.
FR3: Every response carries X-Correlation-Id: the incoming header is echoed (max 128 chars), otherwise a trace identifier is generated.
FR4: Unhandled exceptions and bare status codes are rendered as RFC 7807 problem details (application/problem+json).
FR5: The click writer flushes buffered events on shutdown and retries transient SQLite lock errors with backoff (existing behaviour, now documented and covered).
nonFunctionalRequirements: NFR1: No new external services or non-approved packages (clarified Q2).
NFR2: Limits are configurable (RateLimiting:CreatePerMinute, default 30) (clarified Q3).
NFR3: Existing endpoints keep their contracts; existing tests pass unchanged except for test infrastructure raising the limit.
NFR4: Operability checks (health, readiness, rate limiting, graceful shutdown, problem details, correlation id, run docs) are verifiable from the code base.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: With CreatePerMinute=3, five rapid POST /api/links yield exactly three 201 and two 429.
AC2: GET /unknown-code still returns 404 under the create limit (redirects are not throttled).
AC3: GET /health/ready returns 200 against a working database.
AC4: A request with X-Correlation-Id: test-corr-123 gets the same value back; a request without it gets a non-empty generated id.
AC5: A validation failure returns application/problem+json with status 400.
AC6: The complete pre-existing test suite passes.
assumptions: A1: Per-instance in-process rate limiting is acceptable for a single-instance deployment (Q2/Q3).
A2: Durability work (EF migrations) remains a documented follow-up, not part of this change (Q1 chose operational resilience).
